speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) what are the implications of recent significant partnerships, investments and aid which our ASEAN neighbours have been receiving from China, especially in areas that will compete with Singapore's strategic economic engines, such as ports; and (b) what are the Ministry's plans to ensure that our industries and companies stay ahead and continue to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our economic agencies also work with industry partners and trade associations to track regional developments and identify opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This is not something new for Singapore and we will press on with efforts to enhance productivity, innovation and competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To ensure that our industries and companies remain well-positioned for growth, the Government adopts a range of strategies across sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Specifically on ports, which the Member had highlighted, the Ministry of Transport will elaborate later on on our efforts to keep our port competitive by investing in technology and automation to improve productivity and service levels.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In doing so, these ITMs take stock of the external trends and domestic concerns affecting each industry, some of which the Member has referred to in his question, in order to provide industry-focused support to companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One aspect of the question I asked was about China's investments in ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Certainly, competition for us is not new in the region.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, what is different is that instead of being local government-led, this time round, there is also added support from an external government as well, and Chinese state-owned enterprises.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In a certain sense, the level of competition and most of the industry's concerns would be different.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would there be tweaks by CFE to look into this new dynamic that recently arose?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I do not propose to go into the CFE's recommendations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I will make this point: in terms of investments and economic development in the region, in an era of globalisation and increasing connectivity, when we are seeing more Chinese companies go abroad,  they are not just from China but  from other parts of the world as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are no stranger to investments from the United States and Europe.
